title: You do not know. Allah may bring something new.
subtitle: Even an ending is given room to change
then: Ibn Umar once divorced his wife at the wrong time, and the Prophet ﷺ was angry and told him to take her back. This surah set out the waiting period, and the wife stays in the home during it. Ibn Kathir says the wisdom is that {reward}the husband may regret it and Allah may place in his heart a wish to continue{/reward}.
now: A fight with your spouse, your brother, your best friend. You say "we are done" and you mean it. {idea}Allah built in a pause, even for divorce.{/idea} {reward}You do not know what He might bring about after a few quiet weeks.{/reward}
old: Once it is broken, there is no point waiting.
new: Allah leaves room for change even in endings, so I should not rush to close every door.
try: If you are in a fight with someone close, wait one full day before saying anything final.

title: Keep kindly or part kindly, and Allah makes a way out.
subtitle: Taqwa in the hardest family moment

picture.label: At the end of the wait

row.title: hurt them on the way out

then: Ibn Kathir says at the end of the waiting period the husband either keeps the marriage with kindness, or parts {reward}without abusing, cursing or shaming her{/reward}. Ibn Mas'ud called "whoever has taqwa, Allah makes a way out for him" {idea}the greatest verse of relief in the Quran{/idea}.
now: A business partnership ending. A flatmate moving out. A marriage coming apart. {trap}It is tempting to win the ending, to have the last word.{/trap} {reward}Part with dignity, and leave the way out to Allah.{/reward}
old: If it is ending anyway, I can say what I really think.
new: Even an ending can be done with kindness, and Allah opens a way for those who stay mindful of Him.
try: Think of one relationship that ended badly. Make a dua for that person today.

title: Provision from where you never expected.
subtitle: He is enough for whoever relies on Him
then: Ibn Abbas rode behind the Prophet ﷺ, who taught him: {idea}be mindful of Allah and He will protect you; if you ask, ask Allah{/idea}. If all people gathered to help or harm you, they could only do what Allah wrote. Ibn Kathir says {reward}Allah has set a measure for all things{/reward}.
now: Rent is due Friday and your account is nearly empty. You have done the sums ten times. {reward}Help often comes from a door you never thought to look at.{/reward} {idea}Do your part, then let Him be enough.{/idea}
old: If I cannot see where the money will come from, it will not come.
new: Allah provides from places I cannot see, and He is enough for me.
try: Write down one worry about provision, then say hasbiyallah and do one practical step toward it.

title: Whoever is mindful of Allah, He makes their matter easy.
subtitle: No one's situation was left out
then: After the waiting period was set in Surah Al-Baqarah, Ubayy bin Ka'b said some women had not been mentioned. Ibn Kathir says this verse came to cover them. Subay'ah al-Aslamiyyah asked the Prophet ﷺ about her own case after her husband died. The verse closes: {reward}whoever has taqwa, Allah makes their matter easy{/reward}.
now: Your life does not fit the neat example in the lecture. The family situation is complicated, the timing is strange. {idea}You are not invisible.{/idea} {reward}Ask the people of knowledge, stay mindful of Allah, and He makes the way easier.{/reward}
old: My situation is too complicated for religion to speak to.
new: Allah addressed people with unusual cases, and He makes it easy for whoever is mindful of Him.
try: If you have a question about your faith you have been too shy to ask, ask a trusted scholar or teacher this week.

title: This is Allah's command, sent down to you.
subtitle: Taqwa wipes sins and makes the reward great
then: The third promise to the mindful in this surah. Ibn Kathir says this is Allah's command sent through His Messenger ﷺ, and whoever keeps it with taqwa, {reward}Allah removes what he fears and multiplies his reward even for the little good he does{/reward}.
now: You are trying to do the right thing in a messy family situation, and it feels like you are the only one being fair. {reward}Allah sees that effort.{/reward} {idea}Small acts of fairness are not lost, they are multiplied.{/idea}
old: Being fair when others are not is a loss for me.
new: Staying mindful of Allah wipes my mistakes and makes even small good great.
try: Do one small fair thing today for someone who has not been fair to you.

title: Do not harm them to make life tight for them.
subtitle: Fairness when a family is coming apart

key.label: How to treat the other side

then: Ibn Kathir explains that the divorced wife is housed according to what the husband can afford. Qatadah said: even if only a corner of the house. Muqatil said {trap}do not annoy her to force her to pay her way out{/trap}. The couple are told to {reward}work things out between them in a good way{/reward}, so no one is harmed over the child.
now: Co-parenting after a split. Arguments about money, pick-ups, holidays. {trap}It is easy to use the kids or the money as pressure.{/trap} {idea}The verse says: settle it with decency.{/idea} {reward}Neither side wins by making the other's life tight.{/reward}
old: In a dispute, I have the right to make things hard for them.
new: Even in a split, Allah asks me not to squeeze or harm the other person.
try: In any disagreement today, ask yourself: am I trying to solve this, or to make them suffer?

title: After hardship, Allah will bring ease.
subtitle: Each gives from what they have
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}Allah burdens no one beyond what He has given them{/reward}. Then the promise: ease after hardship, which he calls a sure promise Allah never breaks. He tells of a poor wife who kept saying "wait, Allah will provide", and found her oven full.
now: Your friends' families go on holidays. You are counting every penny for school shoes. {idea}Allah only asks you to give from what you have.{/idea} {reward}And He promised that this tight season is followed by ease.{/reward}
old: I am failing because I cannot give what others give.
new: Allah asks only from what He gave me, and ease is promised after this hardship.
try: Write down one hard thing you are going through and next to it write: ease is coming. Keep it somewhere you will see it.

title: How many towns rebelled against their Lord's command.
subtitle: After the laws, a reminder of what defiance costs
then: Right after the rulings on divorce and family, the surah reminds its hearers of earlier towns. Ibn Kathir says they {trap}rebelled, rejected and arrogantly refused to obey Allah{/trap} and would not follow the messengers, so they were called to a severe account.
now: It is easy to treat the "family" verses as small print: who pays, who stays, how long to wait. {idea}The surah puts them next to whole towns that fell.{/idea} {reward}How you treat your family is part of how you obey your Lord.{/reward}
old: Rules about family life are minor details compared to big worship.
new: Allah's commands about my home are as serious as any other command.
try: Think of one thing you owe someone in your family, time, money, or respect, and give it today.

title: They tasted what they chose, and it ended in loss.
subtitle: Regret that comes when it no longer helps
then: Ibn Kathir says these towns {trap}tasted the evil consequences of their defiance and regretted their actions when regret no longer helped{/trap}. The end of their affair was loss.
now: You know the feeling of saying sorry after the damage is done: the friend who has already moved on, the parent who has passed away. {reward}The verse is a gift because it comes early.{/reward} {idea}Regret today can still change something.{/idea}
old: I will feel sorry about it later if I need to.
new: Regret only helps while there is still time, and that time is now.
try: Name one thing you will regret if you leave it. Take one step toward fixing it before tonight.

title: People of understanding, Allah has sent you a reminder.
subtitle: Learn from them so you do not become them
then: Ibn Kathir explains the address: {idea}O you who have sound understanding, do not be like them{/idea}, or you will suffer what they suffered. And Allah has sent down {reward}a Reminder, this Quran{/reward}, which He also promised to preserve.
now: You are smart. You read, you analyse, you can argue any side online. {idea}The Quran calls the wise ones those who actually take the warning.{/idea} {reward}The Reminder is already in your hands, on your phone, on the shelf.{/reward}
old: Being intelligent means I can judge religion for myself.
new: Real understanding is listening to the Reminder and changing because of it.
try: Read one page of the Quran today with the question: what is this asking me to change?

title: From the darkness into the light.
subtitle: A messenger reciting clear verses
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah brings believers {trap}out of the darkness of disbelief and ignorance{/trap} {reward}into the light of faith and knowledge{/reward}. He calls revelation light because of the guidance it brings, and also Ruh, a spirit, because it brings hearts to life.
now: A long, low season. Grief, or a habit that has swallowed your evenings, or just numbness. {idea}Darkness is plural in this verse. So are the ways in.{/idea} {reward}The way out is one light, and it is recited to you.{/reward}
old: I have been in this dark place too long to get out.
new: Allah's verses are a light that can bring me out of any darkness.
try: Listen to one surah tonight before sleep, in a dark room, and let it be the light in it.

title: Seven heavens, and of the earth the like of them.
subtitle: The surah of family law ends on the cosmos

row.title: the same Lord
sub: runs the sky and your home

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah ends this surah by asserting {idea}His perfect power and infinite greatness{/idea}, so that the religion He legislated is honored and lived. He cites the hadith that whoever wrongly takes even a hand span of land {trap}will carry it down through seven earths{/trap}.
now: The surah began with a quarrel in one house and ends with seven heavens. {idea}The One whose command moves between the skies is the One watching how you split the bills and speak to your ex.{/idea} {reward}And His knowledge surrounds all of it.{/reward}
old: Allah is great in the universe, but my home life is my own business.
new: The Lord of seven heavens knows and cares about how I treat people in my home.
try: Tonight, step outside, look at the sky for one minute, and then go inside and be gentle with whoever is there.
